channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Dushanbe to Host International Forum on Digital Transformation and AI
item.description: An international forum, 'Taj Tech – 2026', will be held in Dushanbe on September 29-30. It will focus on digital transformation, artificial intelligence, innovation, startup ecosystems, and international technological cooperation. The event aims to showcase Tajikistan's national potential in these fields.

item.title: Kazakhstan's QazETA System Not Mandatory for Kyrgyz Citizens Yet
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs clarified that the QazETA system for entering Kazakhstan is currently in a pilot phase and not mandatory for Kyrgyz citizens. Entry and stay procedures for Kyrgyz nationals in Kazakhstan remain unchanged. Further information will be provided if migration rules are officially altered.

item.title: ROX Group Plans $1.5 Billion Investment in Uchtepa City Project in Tashkent
item.description: Vietnam's ROX Group plans to invest $1.5 billion in the Uchtepa City project in Tashkent. The multi-sector investment group, established in 1996, discussed potential projects in real estate, energy, finance, and tourism with Uzbek officials. The Uchtepa City complex will feature business centers, residences, and new infrastructure.

item.title: Record wheat yield of 10 tons per hectare achieved in Talas region
item.description: A wheat yield of 10 tons per hectare was harvested in the Manas district of Talas region in 2026, marking one of the highest indicators nationwide. The Ministry of Water Resources, Agriculture, and Processing Industry reported this. The average wheat yield across Kyrgyzstan is 50-55 centners per hectare, making the Manas district's yield nearly double the national average.

item.title: CSTO sees expediency in resuming work with OSCE, says Secretary General
item.description: The Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) sees expediency in resuming cooperation with the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE), according to CSTO Secretary General Talatbek Masadykov. He noted a meeting with OSCE Secretary General Feridun Sinirlioğlu in May, expressing belief in the OSCE's potential to strengthen European security. Masadykov also commented on potential dialogue with NATO.

item.title: UN Reports Record High in International Money Transfers, Exceeding Aid and FDI
item.description: International money transfers to low- and middle-income countries are projected to reach a record $728.6 billion in 2025, according to a UN International Fund for Agricultural Development report. This figure surpasses official development assistance and foreign direct investment, highlighting remittances as a crucial financial lifeline for households.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva Presented with Major Architectural Projects in Tashkent
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva, head of the Presidential Administration, met with initiators of major architectural projects, urbanists, and specialists in Tashkent. She emphasized the need for careful planning to address urban development, ecological concerns, and infrastructure strain, ensuring new constructions benefit the city without causing imbalance.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to commission over 100 educational facilities by end of 2026
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to open more than 100 educational facilities by the end of 2026, according to the Ministry of Education. This includes 34 schools and 28 kindergartens commissioned on September 11, 2026. An additional 58 facilities, comprising 49 new schools and seven kindergartens, plus two renovated schools, are scheduled for completion by year-end.

item.title: Kyrgyz MP questions procurement of LiXiang cars for water ministry
item.description: Member of Parliament Ulan Bakasov questioned the necessity of purchasing three hybrid LiXiang cars for the Ministry of Water Resources, Agriculture, and Processing Industry. The deputy minister stated the cars are for the ministry's three vehicles in Bishkek, funded by a World Bank project. He explained that LiXiang L6 and L9 models meet requirements, with tenders to be announced.

item.title: Uzbekistan national football team to play Syria in Tashkent
item.description: The Uzbekistan national football team will play against Syria in Tashkent. Additionally, the team is scheduled to compete against Iran and South Korea during the September-October FIFA international windows.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon travels to Seoul for Central Asia-Korea summit
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon departed for Seoul on September 15 to attend the first "Central Asia-South Korea" summit. The meeting aims to foster cooperation between the region and South Korea.

item.title: CSTO Secretary General suggests possibility of dialogue with NATO
item.description: The Secretary General of the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO), Imangali Tasmagambetov, stated that the organization does not rule out the possibility of developing dialogue with NATO. He noted concerns over NATO's military infrastructure near CSTO borders and emphasized the CSTO's strategic interest in peace and cooperation.

item.title: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev meets with Speaker of the Korean National Assembly
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Speaker Cho Jung-sik of the Korean National Assembly during his state visit to South Korea. They discussed strengthening bilateral strategic partnership, parliamentary cooperation, and implementing agreements in trade, investment, and cultural exchange.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea agree to hold parliamentary diplomacy events in 2027
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev met with Korean National Assembly Speaker Cho Jong-sik. They agreed to hold several events focused on parliamentary diplomacy in 2027, marking the 35th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Uzbekistan and South Korea.

item.title: US Sanctions on Iran Could Impact Dushanbe-Tehran Relations, Media Reports
item.description: New US sanctions against Iran may affect trade and banking operations between Dushanbe and Tehran, according to an American media outlet. The sanctions are expected to impact the transfer of goods, fuel, and financial transactions.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Competition Committee Launches Case Against Regional Power Grid
item.description: Uzbekistan's Competition Development and Consumer Rights Protection Committee has initiated proceedings against regional power grid companies for unlawfully collecting 5.5 billion soms from entrepreneurs. These charges relate to fees for reconnecting electricity supply after debt settlement, which were abolished by presidential decree and government resolutions.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Establishes Waste Recycling Registry to Promote Circular Economy
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Natural Resources is creating a digital registry for waste recyclers to support sustainable development and producer responsibility. Officials are inspecting companies processing paper, plastic, and textiles. The ministry urges recyclers to obtain licenses to avoid penalties.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Install 44,000 Smart Electricity Meters in Toktogul and Nooken Districts
item.description: Kyrgyzstan plans to install 44,000 smart electricity meters in Toktogul and Nooken districts by 2026 as part of an automated metering system. Since 2024, 106,000 meters have been installed in the Jalal-Abad region. The system aims for accurate consumption tracking and efficient grid management.

item.title: UN report: Artificial intelligence is transforming mercenary activities
item.description: A new UN report highlights how artificial intelligence is changing mercenary operations. The report, presented to the UN Human Rights Council, suggests a new concept of 'technological mercenaryism,' involving private entities using digital and cyber tools for clients.

item.title: CAREC Tourism Working Group Discusses Sustainable and Transboundary Tourism Development
item.description: The CAREC Tourism Working Group met in Tashkent to boost regional tourism cooperation and set priorities for 2026-2027. Supported by Uzbekistan's Tourism Committee and the ADB, the meeting focused on reviving the working group's activities and implementing a tourism development MoU. Priorities include digitalization, capacity building, and modernizing the 'Visit Silk Road' portal.

item.title: Kazakhstan Restores Rare Animal Species and Combats Poaching
item.description: Kazakhstan is implementing large-scale eco-projects, reintroducing Przewalski's horses and tigers to their historical habitats. The Committee of Forestry and Wildlife of the Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources is involved in issuing permits for CITES-listed species, developing conservation laws, and protecting wildlife inspectors from armed poachers.

item.title: Expert Dialogue Forms Basis for New Central Asia-UK Cooperation Phase
item.description: The first Central Asia-UK Think Tank Forum, held in Tashkent, brought together experts from research institutions, diplomatic corps, and business circles. Organized by the International Institute of Central Asia and ODI Global, the forum aims to elevate relations between Central Asia and the UK, focusing on sustainable development and East-West connectivity.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea to create platform for strategic minerals; exports decrease
item.description: Uzbekistan and South Korea will establish a platform for strategic minerals. In the first seven months of the year, Uzbekistan's exports decreased by 3.6%. Sugar imports increased 2.5 times. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev identified five priority areas for economic cooperation with South Korea.

item.title: Uzbekistan prioritizes ecological responsibility for national development
item.description: Uzbekistan's president has outlined seven national programs for the country's development, emphasizing ecological responsibility. Key goals include transforming attitudes towards water and nature, ensuring environmental sustainability, and expanding the "Green Space" project. Environmental safety is deemed crucial for economic, social, and political progress.

item.title: Unified system to monitor student attendance, safety, and employment in Uzbekistan's universities
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to establish a unified system for managing student campuses and enhancing safety in higher education institutions. The system will include a dedicated directorate for managing living conditions, improving dormitories, developing green areas, and organizing cultural events. "Smart" cameras and a single platform will be implemented.

item.title: Uzbekistan Adopts New Agricultural Approach: From Tradition to Innovation
item.description: Uzbekistan is implementing a new, scientifically-based approach to agriculture, focusing on high-quality production with minimized resource costs. Two major agro-projects in Nishan district are transforming 2,500 hectares of desert land into green areas, cultivating fodder crops and seed potatoes.

item.title: Foreign Marketplaces to Pay VAT on Sales in Uzbekistan Under New Tax Rules
item.description: Foreign online marketplaces selling goods to customers in Uzbekistan will now be subject to new tax regulations, including paying VAT on sales. Amendments to the Law on Electronic Commerce clarify rights and obligations for e-commerce participants and digital goods.

item.title: Regional conference on 'One Health' concept held in Bishkek
item.description: A regional conference on the 'One Health' concept, focusing on combating infectious threats across borders, has opened in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan. Over 150 representatives from Central Asian nations and international organizations are attending. The initiative emphasizes integrating medicine, veterinary science, agriculture, and environmental control to address zoonotic diseases and prevent future epidemics.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea sign documents to strengthen partnership
item.description: Following high-level talks in Seoul, Uzbekistan and the Republic of Korea have signed a package of bilateral documents aimed at deepening cooperation. The agreements cover trade, investment, transport, aviation, agriculture, tourism, artificial intelligence, education, healthcare products, ecology, and climate change mitigation.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea shift focus from investment to technological cooperation
item.description: Uzbekistan and the Republic of Korea are moving towards deeper industrial and technological cooperation, shifting from their previous focus on trade and investment. Key areas include joint production chains, high-tech localization, and resource processing. The goal is to increase annual trade turnover to $4 billion.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Competition Committee launches cases against regional power companies
item.description: Uzbekistan's Competition Committee has initiated cases against regional electricity network companies for illegally collecting 5.5 billion soms from entrepreneurs. The committee identified 965 instances of unlawful reconnection fees. The issue is under comprehensive review with relevant state bodies.

item.title: Uzbek President emphasizes security's impact on investment and business confidence
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev stressed that security directly influences investment attractiveness and business confidence. He stated that economic efforts are insufficient without controlling crime, urging law enforcement to set an example and ensure citizens live without fear.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan allocates 3.1 billion soms for contributions to international organizations
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Cabinet of Ministers has approved contributions totaling 3.1 billion soms to international organizations and integration associations for 2026. The largest share, over 1.9 billion soms, is allocated to the Turkic Investment Fund.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea Elevate Strategic Partnership to New Level
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev's state visit to South Korea marks a new phase in bilateral relations. The countries aim to develop a high-tech hub in Uzbekistan, with $9.6 billion in new investment projects agreed upon. Discussions also covered long-term technological and industrial cooperation.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Economic Growth Reaches 11 Percent in Eight Months
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Gross Domestic Product reached 1.397 trillion soms in eight months, with economic growth at 11 percent, according to Cabinet Chairman Adylbek Kasymaliev. Investments in fixed capital grew by 61.2%, construction by 61%, industry by 8.8%, and agriculture by 6.4%.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea Presidents Affirm Commitment to Special Strategic Partnership
item.description: Presidents Shavkat Mirziyoyev of Uzbekistan and Lee Jae-myung of South Korea met in Seoul, reaffirming their commitment to deepening their special strategic partnership. They noted the growth in trade and investment, with over 700 joint ventures and significant Korean investments exceeding $8 billion in Uzbekistan.

item.title: Bishkek Residents May Receive Loans for Heat Pump Installation
item.description: A meeting in Bishkek discussed a World Bank project to improve air quality in Kyrgyzstan. A key focus is a credit line for households to install heat pumps, enhancing energy efficiency and reducing emissions during the heating season.

item.title: Uzbekistan and South Korea deepen strategic partnership amid global shifts
item.description: Uzbekistan and South Korea are strengthening their strategic partnership, expanding cooperation beyond trade and investment to encompass industrial cooperation. This collaboration is gaining importance amid global geopolitical changes and economic transformations, with Central Asia seen as a promising region for diversification and high-tech development.

item.title: Uzbekistan shifts environmental control from reactive to proactive approach
item.description: Uzbekistan is transforming its environmental oversight from a reactive tool to a proactive system, focusing on risk prediction and impact assessment during planning. The "On Environmental Control" law emphasizes prevention alongside enforcement, reflecting a global shift towards risk-oriented and partner-based supervision.

item.title: Navoiy region develops agriculture through land reclamation and irrigation projects
item.description: The Kanimekh district in Uzbekistan's Navoiy region is developing agriculture by reclaiming abandoned pastures and improving irrigation. Projects include the Kengsoy canal to water 3,800 hectares and a reservoir for 1.6 million cubic meters. Investment is being attracted for crop and livestock feed production.
